Separately, every one of the 17 bound-indicator shapes was run through BOTH lanes before this record, twice: once on the raw declared series (13,317 (case, bar) comparisons) and once with a NaN-carrying composed argument in each series slot (19,686 comparisons). Zero differences at rel-tol 1e-9 in both sweeps. The second sweep is the one that found something: without the finite-tail rule `compute_atr_raw`'s `max(h - l, abs(h - prev_c), abs(l - prev_c))` returns Python's first argument on a NaN `prev_c` while `Math.max` returns NaN -- a real divergence no golden indicator fixture can contain, because no fixture contains a NaN.

rerecorded.proof: Both lanes were run over all 44 cases by `--record` itself (24,575 finite of 25,476 rows, every case non-empty, 48 table entries covered) and `--check` then re-verified every digest. The seven new rows were chosen to separate things that a single case would have conflated: `offset_inside_a_reduction` (`sma(close[2],20)`) and `offset_of_a_reduction` (`sma(close,20)[2]`) have the SAME maxLookback of 22 and DIFFERENT values, so a lane that composed the two orders together would agree on the budget and disagree on the numbers; `offset_change_idiom` pins that `close - close[1]` stays not-computable on bar 0 rather than collapsing to a fabricated 0.0 a user could arm an alert on; `offset_of_a_condition` pins that NaN propagates through the pad rather than the comparison's own `NaN -> 0` rule reaching it; `offset_two_bars_apart` pins that the pad under an operator is the DEEPER of two offsets and not their sum; `offset_zero_is_identity` pins that the parse door FOLDS `x[0]` to `x` rather than emitting a zero-bar node, because one column may have only one canonical tree and `astHash` decides whether an edit force-migrates every binding.
rerecorded.what_moved: NOTHING MOVED. Measured against a snapshot of the previous `digests` map taken BEFORE `--record` ran and compared key by key rather than eyeballed as a diff -- MOVED [] / REMOVED [] / ADDED 7. The log went 37 -> 44 per-ast digests over the same 579 bars at the same 1e-9; `bars`, `bar_count` and `rel_tol` are byte-identical. That is the load-bearing half: the offset node is PURELY ADDITIVE to every tree that does not contain one, and an unmoved digest set is the only evidence of that anybody can re-run. SEPARABLE FROM THE OTHER TWO MOVEMENTS IN THIS WORKING TREE: the indicator agent's 17 -> 37 (the `rerecorded` entry above this one) and its manifest growth 85 -> 102 declared names touched no offset row, and these seven rows touch no function.
rerecorded.why: Phase F6 added the BOUNDED BACKWARD OFFSET as a fifth canonical node type -- `{type:'offset', value:<int >= 1>, args:[<one child>]}`, which `parse.js` produces for the source spelling `EXPR[N]`. `closedTable.json::_no_offset` forbade a backward-index form because "a general `close[n]` turns the repaint linter from a lookback SUM into a dataflow analysis, and it makes a FORWARD reference expressible in the first place". Both halves of that are answered by the SHAPE rather than by a check: the bar count is a NUMBER ON THE NODE with no slot for an expression, and a negative literal is refused AT PARSE (`canonicalise:offset-forward`), so `maxLookback` stays a tree sum (`value + maxLookback(child)`) and a forward reference is inexpressible. Seven cases were owed because `assert_corpus_covers_the_table` and `test_ast_conformance`'s node-type rail both derive their floor from what the corpus exercises, so a fifth node type with no case would have read as coverage.
